architecture.mechanism: Nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond exhibit bright photoluminescence coupled with outstanding photostability and optically addressable spin states, making them stable, non-bleaching fluorescent quantum probes usable as reference standards for extreme ultraviolet (EUV) metrology and semiconductor device analysis.
architecture.intervention: Embed fluorescent nanodiamonds (FNDs) containing NV- centers as in-situ photostable calibration/reference markers at critical optical nodes (reticle plane, wafer plane, and collector optics line-of-sight) inside the ASML Twinscan EXE/NXE system, so their EUV-induced luminescence serves as a stable intensity baseline against which beam dose and optical throughput drift can be continuously re-measured.
architecture.expected_effect: Because the reference signal does not photodegrade, any measured drop in FND emission relative to baseline is attributable to genuine EUV source/optics throughput loss rather than probe decay, enabling early detection of mirror contamination, source power decline, or pellicle degradation while preserving nanometer-scale patterning precision and wafer throughput.
architecture.falsification_test: Mount FND reference markers at the wafer plane of an operating NXE/EXE system, log their NV- photoluminescence against integrated EUV dose over a controlled exposure campaign, and compare against a calibrated absolute EUV power meter; if the FND signal drifts (e.g., >2%) independent of measured beam power, or fails to track known throughput drops, the mechanism is falsified.
